rows.text: The Assembly's news item created on 15 December 2021 states that 'Yesterday Parliament elected Lord Fakafanua and Lord Tu'iha'angana as the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, respectively'; it reports that Lord Fakafanua told the media he is happy to return as Speaker, quotes him ('Being re-elected, I have noticed there is lots of unfinished businesses ...'), and captions a photograph 'Speaker of Parliament, Lord Fakafanua'.
rows.locator: Article header ('Created: 15 December 2021'); the photograph caption after paragraph 2; the paragraphs beginning 'Yesterday Parliament elected' and 'Lord Fakafanua told the media'
rows.uncertainty: The Assembly's election of its Speaker, recorded separately from any royal appointment (none was found for this Assembly) and from any oath. The vote's day is not fixed: the item is dated 15 December but says 'Yesterday'; the Interim Speaker's notice already in the packet scheduled the Speaker's election for the 15 December meeting, and the capture was made at 00:07 UTC on 16 December. The claim is attested on the item's date and no day is inferred. 'Re-elected' and 'return as Speaker' are the item's words and are not used to join this term to the 2017 holder.
